facts.text: In February 1660, Shaistakhan left Ahmadnagar and entered the Pune province.
facts.quote: In February 1660, Shaistakhan left from Ahmadnagar and entered the Pune province.

facts.text: Shaistakhan encamped at Chakan; its Killedar Firangoji Narsala resisted strongly, but the Mughals captured the fort.
facts.quote: He encamped at Chakan. Firangoji Narsala, the Killedar of the fort of Chakan offered a strong resistance to Shaistakhan's army. Finally, the Mughals captured the fort of Chakan.

facts.text: Shaistakhan set up his camp at Lal Mahal in Pune, where Shivaji Maharaj had lived in his childhood.
facts.quote: Shaistakhan set up his camp at Lal Mahal in Pune where Shivaji Maharaj had lived in his childhood.

facts.text: Two years passed, but Shaistakhan would not leave Pune; his forces looted the people.
facts.quote: These forces looted the people. Two years passed, but he would not think of leaving Pune.

facts.text: On 5 April 1663, Maharaj raided Lal Mahal at night; Shaistakhan lost his fingers.
facts.quote: On 5 April 1663, Maharaj raided Lal Mahal at night with a select band of soldiers. In this raid, Shaistakhan lost his fingers.

facts.text: Shaistakhan shifted his camp to Aurangabad; Aurangzeb transferred him to the province of Bengal.
facts.quote: He left Pune and shifted his camp to Aurangabad. ... Aurangzeb transferred him to the province of Bengal.

facts.text: Surat was a big, rich trade centre and port under Mughal control; the British and Dutch had factories there.
facts.quote: Surat was a big trade centre and port under Mughal control. The British and Dutch had their factories there. ... It was a rich city.

facts.text: Inayat Khan, the Subhedar of Surat, could not resist; Maharaj took plenty of wealth without bothering the common people.
facts.quote: Inayat Khan, the Subhedar of Surat could not put up any resistance. Maharaj obtained plenty of wealth from Surat without bothering the common people.

facts.text: Aurangzeb sent Mirzaraja Jaisingh, an experienced and powerful Rajput Sardar; Jaisingh came to Pune.
facts.quote: Aurangzeb sent Mirzaraja Jaisingh, an experienced and powerful Rajput Sardar. Jaisingh came to Pune.

facts.text: Jaisingh urged the Portuguese of Goa and Vasai, the Dutch of Vengurla, the British of Surat and the Siddis of Janjira to start a naval campaign.
facts.quote: To the Portuguese of Goa and Vasai, the Dutch of Vengurla, the British of Surat and the Siddis of Janjira, Jaisingh suggested that they should start a naval campaign against Maharaj.

facts.text: When Jaisingh and Dilerkhan besieged Purandar, Murarbaji Deshpande fought with great courage and died a hero's death.
facts.quote: Jaisingh and Dilerkhan laid siege to the fort of Purandar. When the Mughals put the fort of Purandar under siege, Murarbaji Deshpande fought with the greatest of courage. He died a hero's death.

facts.text: The Treaty of Purandar between Jaisingh and Maharaj was signed in June 1665.
facts.quote: A treaty between Jaisingh and Maharaj was signed in June 1665. It is known as the 'Treaty of Purandar'.

facts.text: By the treaty, Maharaj gave the Mughals twenty-three forts and territories yielding four lakh hons a year; Aurangzeb ratified it.
facts.quote: Maharaj gave to the Mughals, twenty-three of his forts and the adjoining territories yielding an annual revenue of four lakh hons. He also assured the Mughals of help against the Adilshahi. The Treaty was ratified by Aurangzeb.

facts.text: Jaisingh's campaign against the Adilshahi failed; he proposed that Maharaj visit Agra and guaranteed his safety.
facts.quote: Maharaj helped Jaisingh but this campaign of Jaisingh was not successful. ... Jaisingh proposed to Shivaji Maharaj that he should visit Agra and meet the Emperor. He guaranteed the safety of Shivaji Maharaj.

facts.text: At Agra, Aurangzeb did not honour Maharaj and put him under house arrest; Maharaj escaped and reached Rajgad.
facts.quote: Aurangzeb did not treat him with due honour at his court. ... The Emperor then put him under house arrest. ... He adroitly escaped from Agra and reached Maharashtra safely after a few days. He reached Rajgad.

facts.text: Prince Sambhaji went to Agra with Maharaj; on the return he was left at Mathura and later brought safely to Rajgad.
facts.quote: He was accompanied by Prince Sambhaji ... While returning from Agra, he had left Sambhaji Raje at Mathura. Later, Prince Sambhaji was brought safely to Rajgad.

facts.text: While Maharaj was away, Veermata Jijabai and his associates looked after the administration of Swaraj.
facts.quote: While Maharaj was away from Swaraj, Veermata Jijabai and the associates of Shivaji Maharaj looked after the administration of Swaraj.

facts.text: Maharaj attacked Ahmadnagar and Junnar and recaptured Sinhgad, Purandar, Lohagad, Mahuli, Karnala and Rohida.
facts.quote: Maharaj attacked the Mughal territories of Ahmadnagar and Junnar. Then, he recaptured several forts such as Sinhgad, Purandar, Lohagad, Mahuli, Karnala, and Rohida, one after the other.

facts.text: After attacking Surat a second time, Maharaj defeated the Mughal Sardar Daudkhan at Vani-Dindori in Nashik district.
facts.quote: Then Maharaj attacked Surat for a second time. While returning from Surat, he fought a great battle with the Mughals at Vani-Dindori in Nashik district. Maharaj defeated the Mughal Sardar Daudkhan in the great battle.

facts.text: Moropant Pingale captured Triambakgad near Nashik.
facts.quote: After that, Moropant Pingale captured Triambakgad near Nashik.

facts.text: Tanaji Malusare, Moropant Pingale and Prataprao Gujar contributed to these offensives.
facts.quote: Sardars such as Tanaji Malusare, Moropant Pingale, Prataprao Gujar etc. made a valuable contribution in these offensives.

facts.text: Krishnaji Anant Sabhasad, a contemporary chronicler, wrote that Maharaj took twenty-seven forts in four months.
facts.quote: Krishnaji Anant Sabhasad, a contemporary chronicler, thus describes this campaign : '(He) took as many as twenty-seven forts in four months and earned a great reputation for himself'.

facts.text: On 6 June 1674, Shivaji Maharaj was coronated at Raigad by Gagabhatt, a learned Pandit.
facts.quote: On 6 June 1674, he had himself coronated at Raigad by Gagabhatt, a learned Pandit.

facts.text: The founding of the Swaraj involved a struggle of over thirty years; a coronation was needed for recognition as a sovereign independent State.
facts.quote: The founding of the Maratha Swaraj involved a relentless struggle for over thirty years. Maharaj realised that now it was necessary for the Swaraj to win general recognition as a sovereign independent State. For this, a formal coronation was necessary.

facts.text: As a symbol of sovereignty, the Rajyabhisheka shaka (coronation era) was started.
facts.quote: As a symbol of sovereignty, the Rajyabhisheka shaka (the coronation era) was started. Maharaj became the founder of a new era.

facts.text: Coins minted for the coronation: a gold Hon and a copper Shivrai, inscribed 'Shri Raja Shivachhatrapati'.
facts.quote: special coins were minted - a gold coin called Hon and a copper coin called Shivrai with the legend 'Shri Raja Shivachhatrapati' inscribed on them.

facts.text: Royal correspondence (Rajpatra) carried the words 'Kshatriyakulaavantansa Shri Raja Shivachhatrapati'.
facts.quote: Thereafter, all royal correspondence (Rajpatra) carried the words, 'Kshatriyakulaavantansa Shri Raja Shivachhatrapati'.

facts.text: The Rajya-vyavahara-kosha was a dictionary giving Sanskrit alternatives for Persian words.
facts.quote: A dictionary showing Sanskrit alternatives for Persian words was prepared. It is known as Rajya-vyavahara-kosha.

facts.text: Sabhasad wrote: 'It was no mean achievement for a Maratha King to become such a great Chhatrapati.'
facts.quote: Sabhasad (a contemporary chronicler) writes, 'It was no mean achievement for a Maratha King to become such a great Chhatrapati.'

facts.text: On 24 September 1674, a second coronation was performed under Nischalpuri Gosavi; Maharaj honoured both the Vedic and Tantric traditions.
facts.quote: Shortly after this, on 24 September 1674 Shivaji Maharaj had his second coronation performed under the guidance of Nischalpuri Gosavi. There were two traditions of religious ceremonies in India - Vedic and Tantric. Maharaj honoured both the traditions and had two coronation ceremonies performed.

facts.text: Prince Sambhaji Raje was 17 years old at the coronation and described it in the treatise 'Budhabhushanam'.
facts.quote: Prince Sambhaji Raje was 17 years old at the time of the coronation of Shivaji Maharaj. He has described the coronation ceremony in the treatise 'Budhabhushanam'.

facts.text: The coronation throne had eight bejewelled pillars and was made of thirty-two 'mann' of gold.
facts.quote: There were eight bejewelled pillars on eight sides of the throne. This throne made of thirty-two 'mann' of gold had been studded with precious jewels.

facts.text: In October 1677, three years after the coronation, Maharaj began a campaign of the South, met the Qutubshah at Golconda and made a treaty of friendship.
facts.quote: Three years after the coronation, in October 1677, Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj undertook a campaign of the South. He went to Golconda. There he called on the Qutubshah. He entered into a treaty of friendship with him.

facts.text: Maharaj won Bengaluru and Hoskote in Karnataka and Jinji and Vellore in Tamil Nadu; Raghunath Narayan Hanamante became chief administrator there.
facts.quote: Maharaj won Bengaluru, Hoskote in Karnataka, Jinji Vellore, etc. forts in today's Tamil Nadu and some other territories of Adilshah. He appointed Raghunath Narayan Hanamante the chief administrator to look after these conquered territories.

facts.text: Vyankoji, the half-brother of Shivaji Maharaj, was ruling at Tanjavur; its Saraswati Mahal library is world famous.
facts.quote: Vyankoji, the half-brother of Shivaji Maharaj, was then ruling at Tanjavur. ... The Saraswati Mahal library there is world famous.

facts.text: Later, Chhatrapati Rajaram Maharaj took shelter in Jinji and ran the administration of Swaraj from there.
facts.quote: the then Chhatrapati Rajaram Maharaj had to leave Maharashtra for reasons of safety. At that time, he took shelter in this southern fort of Jinji and ran the administration of Swaraj from there.

facts.text: Shivaji Maharaj passed away on Raigad on 3 April 1680, at the age of fifty.
facts.quote: Shivaji Maharaj passed away on Raigad on 3 April 1680. His death at the age of fifty was a great loss for Swaraj.

facts.text: The Surat campaign was a stunning blow to Emperor Aurangzeb's prestige.
facts.quote: His campaign of Surat was completely successful. This campaign was a stunning blow to Emperor Aurangzeb's prestige.
